column1: Zod v4: does a top-level `.refine()` / `.superRefine()` on `z.object({...})` run when one of the object's FIELDS fails to parse?
column2:
Yes — in Zod v4 it runs even when fields fail. It receives the parsed-so-far data (a field that failed its own `.min()` still passes its raw value through), so cross-field errors and field errors surface together in one safeParse.

Zod v3 GATED it: the refine ran only if the whole object parsed first. So don't assume a refine is dormant just because a field is failing — that reasoning was v3-only.

column1: Zod: reach for `.superRefine((d, ctx) => …)` over two chained `.refine()`s when?
column2:
When one pass must raise SEVERAL issues, or target different `path`s: `ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", message, path })` can be called many times.

It is NOT a way to "un-gate" checks — in v4 two `.refine()`s already both run regardless of field failures. superRefine is consolidation/ergonomics only.

column1: JS: `const [, a, b] = arr` skip-first destructuring — what breaks if you `.filter()` a regex match array before destructuring it?
column2:
The leading `,` skips index 0. On a raw regex `match`, index 0 is the full-match string (correctly skipped). But `match.map(Number).filter(Number.isInteger)` DROPS that NaN slot — now index 0 is a real capture group, the skip-comma eats it, everything shifts left, and the last var reads past the end → undefined.

Fix: drop the leading comma, OR don't filter — convert per group: `const [, sh, sm, eh, em] = match; Number(sh)…`. A skip-comma is bound to one array shape; a transform that changes the shape invalidates it.

column1: `isPossiblePhoneNumber(v)` (libphonenumber-js) rejects `89001234567` — why, and how to accept how Russians actually type?
column2:
With no country it parses as international → only `+`-prefixed E.164 passes; bare `8…`/`9…` national formats fail. Pass the object form `isPossiblePhoneNumber(v, { defaultCountry: "RU" })` so national formats parse.

This is MORE permissive for local users, not stricter. `isPossiblePhoneNumber` = length plausibility; `isValidPhoneNumber` = real number ranges. Import from `libphonenumber-js`, NOT `react-phone-number-input` (that's the React UI lib).

column1: HTML forms: does a field with `display:none` (or inside a hidden container) get excluded from `FormData` / submission?
column2:
No. Only `disabled` removes a control from FormData; visibility (`display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, a hidden ancestor) does NOT — a hidden field keeps its value and still submits.

Consequence: toggling a field out of view without clearing its value leaks stale input into the payload (e.g. select a pickup point, switch to address mode → both ship). Fix = clear the value (or set `disabled`) on toggle, not just hide it.

column1: Validation at a notify/webhook endpoint that fires AFTER the real order is already committed upstream — reject bad input, or pass through?
column2:
Rejecting can't prevent the bad order (it already exists); a 400 only loses the manager notification. So parse for SHAPE (enough to interpolate/narrow safely) but don't police CONTENT with cross-field refines or enums on display-only values.

Strictness is protective only where rejection blocks the bad thing — here rejection IS the failure mode. Caveat: if the endpoint is publicly reachable, keep enough validation that a direct caller can't crash it or inject garbage into the message.
